dmai: Divisia Monetary Aggregates Index

Overview

dmai builds monetary aggregates from their components (currency, demand deposits, savings and time deposits, …) by the methods of index number theory:

  • dmai(): the Divisia index of Barnett (1980), which weights every component by its share in the expenditure on monetary services priced by its user cost (Barnett 1978); also the variant with simple growth rates (Hancock), the Fisher ideal index, the simple sum and the currency equivalent index of Rotemberg, Driscoll and Poterba (1995), each with the dual user-cost price index;
  • dmai_compare(): every method on the same data;
  • dmai_user_cost(): the user costs and weights of the components;
  • dmai_moments(): the Divisia second moments of Barnett and Serletis (1990);
  • ggplot2 graphics, a plain-language interpretation of every result (dmai_interpret()), the references of every method (dmai_cite()) and an application that runs all of this without code (dmai_app()).

Version 1.0.0 keeps the function, arguments and results of version 0.5.0, with one correction: the growth DMAI now uses natural logarithms by default, so it is a growth rate in percent (0.5.0 used base 10, which gives 0.434 times that; logbase = 10 reproduces it). The package no longer depends on the tidyverse, and its index formulas reproduce the published values of the Consumer Price Index Manual (ILO et al. 2004, Chapter 19).

Installation 

install.packages("dmai")
# development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/dmai")

Quick start

The example data money_sim are simulated monthly components of a broad money aggregate with their rates and a benchmark rate (rb).

library(dmai)
data(money_sim)
fit <-
  dmai(
      .data     = money_sim
    , method    = "Barnett"
    , logbase   = NULL
    , date      = "Date"
    , x         = NULL
    , r         = NULL
    , user_cost = NULL
    , benchmark = "rb"
    , percent   = TRUE
    , base      = 100
    , as_dt     = FALSE
    )
fit

dmai_interpret(
    x   = fit
  , top = 3
  )
Divisia (Barnett) monetary aggregate

From 2005-01-01 to 2024-12-01 the Divisia (Barnett) aggregate grew 11.3% a
year, against 12.8% for the simple sum (1.6 points less).

Findings:
- Largest growth at 2009-03-01, 2021-12-01, 2024-01-01 (2.49, 2.24, 2.17);
  smallest at 2007-06-01, 2012-09-01, 2018-12-01 (-0.71, -0.67, -0.61).
- At the last date the largest weights are x3 (28.1%), x1 (19.5%), x2
  (18.8%).
- The weights moved most for x1 (32.3 to 19.5%), x4 (4.3 to 9.9%), x6 (3.7 to
  8.5%).
- The simple sum overstates money growth: it gives the same weight to
  interest-bearing deposits, which are held largely as savings, as to
  currency and demand deposits.

Recommendations:
- Compare the methods with dmai_compare(); check how the result depends on
  the benchmark rate.
- dmai_moments() shows when the components grow at very different rates.

Sources:
- Barnett, W. A. (1978). The user cost of money. Economics Letters, 1(2),
  145-149. doi:10.1016/0165-1765(78)90051-4
- Barnett, W. A. (1980). Economic monetary aggregates: an application of
  index number and aggregation theory. Journal of Econometrics, 14(1), 11-48.
  doi:10.1016/0304-4076(80)90070-6
- Tornqvist, L. (1936). The Bank of Finland's consumption price index. Bank
  of Finland Monthly Bulletin, 10, 1-8.
- Theil, H. (1967). Economics and Information Theory. North-Holland,
  Amsterdam.
plot(x = fit)
